thread:
olivia: Quick brain dump — for the upcoming benchmark webinar we need a single-sentence lead that ties latency to customer dollars, not just tech. e.g., "A 50ms tail can cost you X in conversions" or similar. thoughts?

james: love that. can we make it less hypothetical? need a real customer scenario or a micromodel example to make the claim feel tangible.

carmen: +1. suggest we use a 'search assistant' demo: show 3 bucket sizes (fast, medium, slow) and map latency -> token cost -> response time -> conversion drop. one slide.

mike: for charts I can produce a 3-panel viz: left = latency distribution (P50/P90/P99), middle = tokens-per-session vs throughput, right = estimated cost-per-1k-reqs. want consistent color palette.

olivia: that sounds perfect. keep axes simple. proposed labels: left x=time(ms), y=percent; middle x=session length (tokens), y=cost; right x=throughput, y=unit $/req.

james: can we also overlay routing options? i.e., show how smart routing (cheap model fallback) shifts the cost curve while slightly widening tail latency.

carmen: yes — add a dashed line for routing offload. callout: "fallback keeps uptime but affects latency distribution".

mike: quick note on data: I'll use bench-run v12 from infra (short context, 2k requests) but I'll synthesize conversion impact using public ecommerce click-rate numbers unless we have customer metrics.

nora: ops_bot: bench-run v12 artifacts are in gs://redwood-bench/v12/ — log file and per-request latencies. use metric names: p50_ms, p90_ms, p99_ms, tokens_total.

mike: grabbing that now. if anyone wants a specific model pair for routing examples, propose using small-quantized (fast) and medium-llama (higher-quality) so we can show cost delta.

james: wording for social posts: short hook, then a one-liner: "How much does 30ms buy you? We measured conversion impact and costs across three serving modes — here's the tradeoff. Join our webinar." Keep CTA to register.

olivia: for the landing page chart we want an interactive slicer (latency threshold). marketing ask: product to provide JSON endpoints for data?

carmen: yes please — mike can commit a small CSV and product can host a static JSON. action: mike to export CSV; nora to make JSON endpoint.

mike: action: exporting CSV with columns (mode, p50_ms, p90_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_session, cost_per_1k) and uploading to gs. target done by EOD today.

nora: action: I'll wire a static JSON at /bench-data/latency-cost-v12.json and point the landing interactive to it. ETA tomorrow AM.

james: copy ideas for webinar title: "Serving Tradeoffs: Latency, Cost, and the Hidden Conversion Tax" — thoughts?

olivia: that's strong. maybe swap 'Tax' for 'Cost' to keep tone less combative. "Hidden Conversion Cost".

carmen: slide deck flow proposed: 1) Demo + ask, 2) Bench methodology, 3) Heatmap + routing tale, 4) Realistic cost scenarios, 5) Q&A + product plug.

mike: I'll produce slides for #3 and #4. will include the 3-panel static PNG + interactive JSON.

ops_bot: Deployment note — CSV uploaded to gs://redwood-bench/v12/latency_cost_export.csv at 1719110000.

olivia: perfect. last: marketing microcopy for ads — two variants: (A) data-first: "We measured latency vs cost — here's what it means for conversion" (B) product-first: "Lower latency without breaking the bank — tools to route and optimize." Which performs better? we'll A/B in the campaign.

james: we'll A/B test both. add tracking params for webinar signups.

olivia: great progress. checklist: mike export (in progress), nora JSON endpoint, mike produces PNGs, carmen drafts slide copy, james writes ad copy + tracking. follow up in tomorrow stand. :sparkles:
